content.title: Copper Just Set a Record. The Market’s Already Having Second Thoughts
content.summary: Copper prices hit a record high in London this week.  Given economic uncertainty in the U.S. and China, the gains may be short lived.  On Thursday, the London Metal Exchange price for a three-month copper contract was down 2.6%, or $287, to $10,897 a metric ton.

content.title: Why the metal powering your electronics is so expensive right now
content.description:
Copper (HG=F) hit a record high earlier today. Disruptions at large mines and disappointing forecasts from leading producers like Glencore (GLEN.L) have led to increased worries over a supply shortage. The industrial metal is used in everything from construction to making electric cars.

content.title: Copper Prices Are Hitting Record Highs
content.summary: Supply concerns have sent copper prices surging, after a series of disruptions at major mines and weaker output forecasts from leading producers.  Three-month copper futures rose as high as $11,146 a metric ton on the London Metal Exchange on Wednesday, before paring gains.

content.title: Glencore Trims Top End of Copper Production Guidance After Output Declines
content.summary: Copper production was down 17% from the comparable period a year prior, the company said. Gold production also dropped while steelmaking-coal continued to rise.

content.title: Metals Traders Are Enjoying Their Most Profitable Year on Record
content.summary: Glencore Plc and Trafigura Group, which have long competed as the two largest players, are both on track for their best year for metal trading, according to people familiar with the matter.  IXM, the third-largest metals trader, has already surpassed last year’s profit and will report its third consecutive record year, according to Chief Executive Officer Kenny Ives.  “There have been some phenomenal opportunities this year,” Ives said at an event at Bloomberg’s London office this week.
